value.body: A tour manager travels with a group from start to finish — on domestic or international package tours — making sure every hotel, coach, meal and visit happens as planned. They handle lost luggage, illness, delays and complaints on the spot. Employers are tour operators that run group tours; much of the work is seasonal.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any graduate; BBA (Tourism) and BTTM are common
items.note: Passport and a clean travel record are needed for international tours

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Days or weeks away on tour; seasonal demand

items.label: Related role
items.value: Licensed tourist guide (licensed separately by government)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start with the operations or sales team of a tour operator and are trained to escort domestic tours first, then international ones. Some operators hire seasonal tour managers on contract.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Languages, including a foreign language for some tours

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior tour manager, operations or product manager.
Long periods away from home are part of the job.
Seasonal and contract work is common, so income can be uneven.
